cases.purpose: Reproduce the check-then-transfer-then-write gap. A ledger-sequence-only append admits the old owner, while the atomic current-snapshot path rejects it.
Show that knowing the exact next ledger sequence does not confer current ownership.
Show that a current ownership snapshot does not make a duplicate or stale ledger position valid.
Reject token reuse and rollback while permitting a strictly increasing, non-contiguous token.
Refute the overbroad claim that a highest-seen sink immediately fences an old owner at authority transfer. It rejects token 1 only after observing token 2.
Permit an exact retry to return its old receipt without a new effect, but reject operation-identifier reuse with changed content.

hypothesis: Fencing tokens have known edge cases that should appear in fault fixtures.
